---
title: "How do I calculate quartiles, the five-number summary, and IQR?"
---

## What the question asks

How do I calculate quartiles, the five-number summary, and IQR?

## Steps in RStudio

1. Sort the data to see their order.

2. Run quantile(x,probs=c(0,.25,.5,.75,1)).

3. Calculate IQR() as Q3 minus Q1.

## Runnable example

```{r}
x <- c(2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16,18)
print(quantile(x,probs=c(0,.25,.5,.75,1)))
print(IQR(x))
print(fivenum(x))
```

## Interpret the result

Using quantile() defaults, Q1 is 6 and Q3 is 14, so the IQR is 8. This five-number example happens to agree with fivenum(), but agreement is not guaranteed for all samples.

## Check before applying this to real data

fivenum() and quantile() can use different quartile conventions; state which was used.
